title: Chevening Scholarships 2027/28
overview: One-year master's degree at any UK university for emerging leaders. Chevening describes the award as fully funded. The 2027/28 round closes on 6 October 2026.
deadline_text: Last cycle closed on 2026-10-06. Next cycle not announced yet.
expected_next_cycle: Recurring programme; previous cycle closed on 2026-10-06.
funding_details: Chevening's site states: 'Chevening Scholarships are fully-funded.'
The itemised list (fees, stipend, flights) was not on the pages read on 2 October 2026.
eligibility: At least 2,800 hours of work experience, acquired after completing the undergraduate degree
That experience must be spread over a minimum of two years
Undergraduate degree completed by October 2024 for this cycle
Eligible work: full-time or part-time employment, voluntary work, paid or unpaid internships
nationality_requirements: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has its own Chevening country page and is open for applications
age_requirement: Not specified on the pages read
experience_requirement: 2,800 hours after the undergraduate degree, over at least two years
application_process: Apply online in the Chevening application system before the deadline
Reading committee assessments from mid-October 2026 to January 2027
Shortlist announced mid-February 2027; interviews March to April 2027
eligibility_reason: Chevening requires 2,800 hours of work gained after the undergraduate degree, over at least two years. The recorded profile shows a degree obtained in 2024 and under one year of short internships, so the requirement is not met this cycle.
potential_issues: No UK visa processing centre and no TB testing facility in the DRC: a successful applicant must travel to another country for both
Those trips are paid by the applicant first; reimbursement of some travel costs is discretionary

DRC country page: there are no UK visa processing centres in the DRC, so a successful scholar must travel to another country to apply for the visa and take the TB test at their own cost, with a discretionary reimbursement of some travel costs
relevance_reason: A strong programme, but the post-degree work-hours rule rules out this round. It becomes realistic once two years of work, volunteering or internships after the degree can be documented.

visa.support: No visa centre in the DRC. Travel to another country to apply; discretionary reimbursement of some travel costs.

upfront_cost_risk: Travel to a third country for the visa application and TB test is paid by the applicant before any reimbursement.
action: No action this round. Keep a dated log of post-degree work, volunteering and internship hours for a later round.
